Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def f(g):
    import copy
    g=[r[:] for r in g]; out=[]; seen=set()
    while True:
        r,c=min((i,j) for i,row in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(row) if x!=0 and x not in seen)
        seen.add(x)
        # bounding box of nonzero same-color cells
        cells=[(i,j) for i,row in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(row) if x!=0]
        rs=[i for i,j in cells]; cs=[j for i,j in cells]
        bgs=[[g[i][j] for j in range(min(cs),max(cs)+1)] for i in range(min(rs),max(rs)+1)]
        out.append(bgs); 
        # clear used cells
        for i,j in cells: g[i][j]=0
        # also remove any stray remaining cells
        newcells=[(i,j) for i,row in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(row) if x!=0]
        if not newcells: break
        # clear them too
        for i,j in newcells: g[i][j]=0
    return out
